svg.font-family: Roboto, Helvetica Neue, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: How sprezzature-figures works
svg.desc: Flow diagram. At the top, your rows or somebody else's chart feed two lanes. The left lane draws: it ranks the kinds that serve your goal, writes the SVG directly with no charting library underneath, and can redraw a screenshot of someone else's chart without inventing its numbers. The right lane audits: a static check reads any SVG at all for labels printed over each other and names off the canvas, then the Ralph Eyeball Loop renders the figure, looks at it, and refines the source. Both meet in one outcome, a figure that is correct before it is beautiful.
svg.text: How sprezzature-figures works
Chart kinds written as SVG by hand, and two ways of looking at what came out.
Your rows, or somebody else's chart
a pandas, polars or Arrow frame, a dict of columns, a CSV. Or a screenshot of a figure that is hard to read.
Make: draw it
Pick the kind, or ask for one
recommend ranks by what the figure is for: comparison, trend,
distribution, composition, relationship, flow, hierarchy,
geography, model evaluation. Readability alone rarely
separates the candidates; the goal is what makes the ranking
decisive.
Write the SVG directly
no charting library underneath, one self-contained generator
per kind, and never ASCII art
Or redraw a picture of a chart
a vision model reads the design, which pixels carry, and never
the numbers, which they usually do not. Every result says
whether it got your data, read it off the image, or fell back
to a demo, and that caption is written onto the figure itself.
An SVG
PNG and PDF through the same renderer that rasterises TikZ
and Mermaid
Audit: the facts first, the judgement after
A static check, on any SVG at all
two labels printed on top of each other, a name running off
the canvas, a value drawn in the colour of the bar behind it, demo
chrome that survived into a real render, a title the generator
was given and quietly dropped.
Say so when there is nothing left to read
a figure whose text was converted to outlines has no text in it,
no screen reader can read it, and every rule would pass
on an empty sight. It reports that rather than returning the empty list
that looks like a pass.
Then the Ralph Eyeball Loop
render it, look at the picture, refine the source, render again.
The model is never allowed to contradict a fact the static
check established.
Findings, each with a severity
error is wrong whoever drew the figure and whatever it
is for; warning is wrong under this house's charter. Exit 1 on any, so
it gates a commit.
A figure that is correct before it is beautiful, and both before it is published
The published work on visualisation linting checks a chart specification, so it has nothing to say about a figure that was not written
in one. This reads the drawing, which is why it can audit a figure it did not draw.
What it will never tell you is that the chart type suits the question. That is a judgement, and the loop is where a model is asked for one.
